name: aadhar-sh
description: aadhar.sh - deploy-time transform only (authoring stays buildless; see build.ts)
comment:workspaces: pnpm does not read npm's `workspaces` field; the package list and the build allowlist live in pnpm-workspace.yaml. See that file, and CLAUDE.md gotcha 29 for why the release script is `deploy:direct` rather than `deploy`.

scripts.dev:remote: bun tools/dev-stage.ts && node tools/gen-remote-config.ts wrangler.dev.jsonc && wrangler dev -c .wrangler.remote.jsonc
scripts.photos:env: uv venv tools/photos/.venv --python 3.12 --allow-existing && uv pip install --python tools/photos/.venv/bin/python -r tools/photos/requirements.txt
scripts.comment:test-node: The same suite under node, kept because a suite that passes on one runtime and fails on another is reporting a fact about the runtime. bun's spec-strict Response found a real defect this way: withSecurityHeaders rebuilds every response, which per Fetch LOCKS the body it was handed, and one test pushed the same case objects through twice. node's undici allows it and bun throws. --test-isolation=none is what makes that comparison honest AND cheap. node's default forks one child per file, so 74 files cost 74 interpreter starts that each re-parse and type-strip the same modules: measured 2026-08-31, 34.5s of CPU against 1.8s, and 18s of the 85s validate job against ~3s. It is also the model bun already uses — probed the same day, a global set in one bun test file is visible in the next — so running node isolated was comparing two runtimes AND two isolation models at once, and a failure could be attributed to the runtime when the process boundary was the cause. Counts are identical either way (551 tests, 542 pass, 9 skipped), and the control is a deliberate failing assertion: it exits 1 and names the file. If a future test needs a fresh process, give it its own file and its own runner line rather than restoring isolation for all 74.
scripts.typecheck: node tools/check-worker-types.ts && node tools/check-browser-types.ts && tsc -p config/tsconfig.sw.json && tsc -p config/tsconfig.lwe-ask.json && tsc -p config/tsconfig.cf-garage.json && node tools/check-tool-types.ts && node tools/check-test-types.ts && node tools/check-ts-coverage.ts

comment:check-fast: Local feedback only: lint, typecheck and test are independent read-only gates, so Bun can run them concurrently. CI keeps them as named sequential steps for legible failures. Do not add build, routes, Lens or perf commands here: several share .build or intentionally run under Node.
comment:engines-node-floor: TWO node floors exist and this field is the HIGHER one: the highest version any constraint in this repo demands. It is NOT the zstd dictionary floor, which is 24, lives beside the check that enforces it as ZSTD_DICTIONARY_NODE_FLOOR in tools/build.ts, and is measured there. Welding the two was right when zstd was the only constraint and went wrong silently the moment source used something newer. What set 26 is Map.prototype.getOrInsertComputed, used in src/worker/inbox.ts, around.ts and census.ts; probed 2026-08-31, it is undefined on node 24.20.0 and 25.4.0 and a function on 26.8.1. PRODUCTION IS UNAFFECTED, which is why nothing caught this: workerd has the method (probed through createTestHarness, and the call works) and /around and /inbox both answer 200. What broke was the repo's own suite under node 24, with 2 failures that read like defects. Note also that 26 EQUALS .node-version, so the floor is now the version CI exercises on every run rather than a claim about a version nothing tests. Raise this whenever a new constraint measures higher, and lower it only with a measurement.
comment:undici: undici arrives only through miniflare, which pins it EXACTLY, so npm cannot move it and dependabot cannot either. An `overrides` block forced 7.29.0 from 2026-08-05 until this commit, for five advisories in the 7.28.0 pin. Both miniflare consumers now ask for 7.29.0 themselves, so the override is gone. The floors are what replace it: `wrangler >= 4.120.0` and `cal`'s `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers >= 0.20.3` are the two versions whose miniflare (5.20260801.1-alpha) carries the fixed pin. Dropping EITHER floor puts 7.28.0 back at the hoisted position, silently, because npm hoists whichever exact pin it resolves first and the vulnerable one wins that race.
comment:exec: A tool NEVER spawns a package manager, and the two perf tools run under NODE rather than bun. Managers: `pnpm exec` refuses on a bun tree outright, and `bun x`/`npx` FETCH what they cannot resolve (measured 2026-08-16 on 1.4.0-canary.1: `bun x wrangler --version` in an empty directory downloaded 4.123.0 from the registry, which is gotcha 29's npx hole wearing bun's name). Spawns go through wranglerCommand() in tools/lib/wrangler-bin.ts, which names node and the pinned entry file. THIS COMMENT USED TO SAY deploy-promote.mjs and perf-budget.mjs already used `bun x --no-install wrangler`. They did not; both still spawned `pnpm exec` when the tree became bun, so the release path and a required check broke on the merge. A comment describing a sweep is not the sweep. Node for the perf tools because the MEASUREMENT must not move with the toolchain: bun 1.4 ships zlib-ng, and on one byte-identical 2.8MB input node gzips to 893,610 bytes against bun's 898,553 (0.55% larger, measured 2026-08-20). Every baseline constant in perf-budget.mjs was set with node's zlib, so running these under bun re-reads the whole series ~1% heavier for free. Shipped bytes are unaffected: brotli and zstd are untouched, which the deploy proved when Cloudflare's content-addressed upload found 0 of 1443 files changed.
comment:overrides: None, since 2026-09-02. The one entry this carried pinned nanoid at ^3.3.17 for GHSA / dependabot #12, reached only through vitest -> vite -> postcss -> nanoid, and cal moved off vitest onto bun:test plus wrangler createTestHarness that day, so the position no longer exists. The lesson stays: bun overrides map a bare name to a version with no selector, so any entry here is unconditional and holds every future resolution of that package until somebody deletes it by hand.
comment:trustedDependencies: bun's spelling of pnpm's `allowBuilds`. Same three packages, same measured reasoning: each ships its platform binary through optionalDependencies and passes its probe with the postinstall blocked, so these are approved to match what the packages intend rather than because anything breaks without them. Semantic note: defining this key REPLACES bun's built-in default allowlist, so the tree stays default-deny exactly as it was.
comment:node-pinned-scripts: THREE scripts still say `node` on purpose, and the reason is measured rather than cautious. `routes:check` boots this repo Worker through wrangler createTestHarness() and then sweeps 142 routes against it over HTTP; under bun that sweep never completes, while under node v26.7.0 it exits 0. RE-TESTED ON BUN 1.4.0 STABLE (2026-08-24), which is what this comment asked for, and the answer is still node, for a NARROWER reason than the one recorded here until that date. TWO THINGS THIS COMMENT USED TO SAY ARE WRONG. It does not hang "with no output and no error": the harness boots, prints its URL, and the child starts and prints its own header before anything stalls. And the hang is NOT at listen(), which was the specific attribution; listen() returns a URL in ~4.2s. THE ACTUAL FAULT IS THE LISTENING SOCKET. A harness hosted in a BUN parent process boots and serves in-process dispatch perfectly and never answers an HTTP request to its own URL. Measured against cal/wrangler.test.toml, one process, one probe: getWorker().fetch() answered 200 on both runtimes, while fetch(url) over the socket answered 200 under node and was still pending when a 15s abort fired under bun. The isolation is what pins it, because either half was a candidate. Swapping ONLY the child runtime: a node parent with a bun child sweeps all 142 routes and exits 0, and a bun parent with a node child hangs. So verify-routes.ts is fine under bun and the harness's socket is not. THE USEFUL HALF, and the reason this is worth more than a red mark: createTestHarness IS usable under bun for anything that dispatches IN-PROCESS. Against cal it booted in 142ms under bun against 269ms under node; getEnv() returned all 17 bindings and vars, a KV put/get/list round-tripped, and introspectWorkflowInstance() returned a live introspector carrying Symbol.asyncDispose whose dispose() ran. Its modifier's mockEvent and forceEventTimeout are read from wrangler's types and NOT exercised, so treat those two as unproven under bun. Reach for the harness in a bun test that talks to bindings; keep node for anything that goes over the wire. cal/test does exactly that since 2026-09-02 (cal/test/harness.ts), which is what retired vitest and @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers from the tree. wrangler, miniflare and workerd are the deploy path AND the route oracle, and they are node-pinned; this is that pin surfacing rather than a bun defect we can route around. Re-test the SOCKET rather than listen(): boot any config under bun, then fetch the URL listen() returned. If that answers, delete this comment and the word node.
comment:engines: bun is the toolchain: it installs, runs every script, runs the tests and runs the build. node is still listed because TWO things measurably require it, both re-testable. (1) wrangler ships a `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang, so the node_modules/.bin shim spawns node; bun CAN run it by invoking the entry directly (`bun ./node_modules/wrangler/bin/wrangler.js` answered 4.123.0 with node shadowed by a failing stub, 2026-08-16), which is the escape hatch if node ever has to go. (2) routes:check sweeps its routes over HTTP against a wrangler createTestHarness() server, and a harness hosted in a bun parent never answers over its listening socket (measured 2026-08-24 on bun 1.4.0 stable; in-process dispatch against the same harness works on both runtimes). See comment:node-pinned-scripts, which carries the isolation and corrects the earlier claim that this was a hang at listen(). Neither is a bun defect to route around; both are the wrangler/miniflare/workerd toolchain being node-pinned.
